title: Mean of Grouped Data: Direct, Assumed Mean & Step-Deviation Methods
description: Master all three methods for computing the arithmetic mean of grouped continuous frequency distributions: (1) Direct Method (x̄ = Σfi·xi / Σfi), (2) Assumed Mean Method (x̄ = a + Σfi·di / Σfi), and (3) Step-Deviation Method (x̄ = a + [Σfi·ui / Σfi] × h). Understand class marks xi = (Upper + Lower) / 2 and deviations.
key_concepts: Class Mark (xi): Midpoint of each class interval: xi = (Upper Class Limit + Lower Class Limit) / 2
Direct Method: x̄ = ( Σ fi · xi ) / ( Σ fi )
Assumed Mean Method: Choose central xi as assumed mean 'a', compute deviations di = xi - a: x̄ = a + ( Σ fi · di ) / ( Σ fi )
Step-Deviation Method: When deviations share common factor 'h' (class width), compute ui = (xi - a) / h: x̄ = a + [ ( Σ fi · ui ) / ( Σ fi ) ] × h
Invariance Principle: All three methods yield the EXACT same numerical answer; step-deviation compresses multi-digit multiplications into single-digit arithmetic!
subtopics: Computing class marks for continuous and discrete intervals
Choosing the optimal assumed mean 'a'
Step-deviation transformation ui = (xi - a) / h
Worked Example 1, Example 2, Example 3 from NCERT

worked_examples.problem:
Example 2 (NCERT): The table below gives the percentage distribution of female teachers in the primary schools of rural areas of various states and union territories (UT) of India. Find the mean percentage of female teachers using all three methods.

Percentage: 15-25 (6), 25-35 (11), 35-45 (7), 45-55 (4), 55-65 (4), 65-75 (2), 75-85 (1). Total states = 35.
worked_examples.solution:
Let class intervals be the percentage ranges, and frequencies 'fi' be the number of states.
Total frequency Σ fi = 35.
Class width h = 25 - 15 = 10.

Step 1: Compute Class Marks (xi) and choose Assumed Mean 'a':
Interval 15-25: x1 = (15+25)/2 = 20, f1 = 6
Interval 25-35: x2 = (25+35)/2 = 30, f2 = 11
Interval 35-45: x3 = (35+45)/2 = 40, f3 = 7
Interval 45-55: x4 = (45+55)/2 = 50, f4 = 4  <-- Choose a = 50
Interval 55-65: x5 = (55+65)/2 = 60, f5 = 4
Interval 65-75: x6 = (65+75)/2 = 70, f6 = 2
Interval 75-85: x7 = (75+85)/2 = 80, f7 = 1

Step 2: Step-Deviation Table (ui = (xi - 50) / 10):
x1 = 20: u1 = -3, f1·u1 = 6 × (-3) = -18
x2 = 30: u2 = -2, f2·u2 = 11 × (-2) = -22
x3 = 40: u3 = -1, f3·u3 = 7 × (-1) = -7
x4 = 50: u4 = 0,  f4·u4 = 4 × 0 = 0
x5 = 60: u5 = 1,  f5·u5 = 4 × 1 = 4
x6 = 70: u6 = 2,  f6·u6 = 2 × 2 = 4
x7 = 80: u7 = 3,  f7·u7 = 1 × 3 = 3

Step 3: Calculate Σ fi·ui:
Negative sum = -18 - 22 - 7 = -47
Positive sum = 4 + 4 + 3 = +11
Σ fi·ui = -47 + 11 = -36.

Step 4: Compute Mean using Step-Deviation Formula:
x̄ = a + [ ( Σ fi·ui ) / ( Σ fi ) ] × h
= 50 + [ (-36) / 35 ] × 10
= 50 - 360 / 35
= 50 - 10.2857 ≈ 39.71%.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Direct method check: Σ fi·xi = 120 + 330 + 280 + 200 + 240 + 140 + 80 = 1390.
x̄ = 1390 / 35 = 39.714% (Exact match!).
Boxed Answer: [ Mean percentage of female teachers = 39.71% ].
concept_questions: Why does step-deviation make calculation faster than direct multiplication?
What is the value of Σ fi·di in the assumed mean method? (-36 × 10 = -360)

common_misconceptions: Forgetting to multiply by 'h' in the step-deviation formula: x̄ = a + (Σfi·ui / Σfi) × h, forgetting 'h' yields an answer around 49 instead of 39.71!
Taking class limits instead of class marks in the direct method.

title: Mode of Grouped Data: Modal Class Identification & Interpolation Formula
description: Understand the concept of Mode as the most frequently occurring value. In grouped data, learn how to identify the Modal Class (class interval having the maximum frequency) and interpolate the exact modal value within that class using the landmark board formula: Mode = l + [ (f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2) ] × h.
key_concepts: Modal Class: The class interval having the highest frequency in the distribution
Interpolation Formula: Mode = l + [ (f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2) ] × h
Variable Definitions: l = lower limit of modal class, h = class size, f1 = frequency of modal class, f0 = frequency of preceding class, f2 = frequency of succeeding class
Denominator Identity: 2f1 - f0 - f2 = (f1 - f0) + (f1 - f2) (Sum of the frequency drop-offs on either side of the peak!)
Boundary Constraint: The calculated mode MUST lie strictly within the modal class interval [l, l + h]!
subtopics: Locating the modal class in grouped distributions
Physical meaning of (f1 - f0) and (f1 - f2) as directional pull on the mode
Worked Example 4 and Example 5 from NCERT

worked_examples.problem:
Example 5 (NCERT): A survey conducted on 20 households in a locality by a group of students resulted in the following frequency table for the number of family members in a household:
Family size: 1-3 (7), 3-5 (8), 5-7 (2), 7-9 (2), 9-11 (1).
Find the mode of this data.
worked_examples.solution:
Given distribution:
Class intervals: 1-3, 3-5, 5-7, 7-9, 9-11
Frequencies: 7, 8, 2, 2, 1.

Step 1: Identify the Modal Class:
The maximum frequency is 8, which corresponds to the class interval 3-5.
Therefore, Modal Class = 3 - 5.

Step 2: Extract variables for the mode formula:
Lower limit of modal class l = 3
Class size h = 5 - 3 = 2
Frequency of modal class f1 = 8
Frequency of preceding class f0 = 7 (for class 1-3)
Frequency of succeeding class f2 = 2 (for class 5-7).

Step 3: Apply Mode Interpolation Formula:
Mode = l + [ (f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2) ] × h
Substitute values:
Mode = 3 + [ (8 - 7) / (2(8) - 7 - 2) ] × 2
= 3 + [ 1 / (16 - 9) ] × 2
= 3 + [ 1 / 7 ] × 2
= 3 + 2 / 7
= 3 + 0.286 = 3.286.

Step 4: Sanity Check:
3.286 lies inside the modal class 3-5 (Valid!).
[ROUGH_WORK]
2 / 7 = 0.2857...
3 + 0.286 = 3.286 family members.
Boxed Answer: [ Mode of the data = 3.286 (or 23/7) ].
concept_questions: Why does the mode shift towards 3 rather than 5? (Because f0 = 7 is much closer to 8 than f2 = 2)
What is the frequency of the modal class?

Selecting the modal class based on class mark instead of highest frequency.

title: Median of Grouped Data: Cumulative Frequencies, Median Class & Empirical Relation
description: Understand the Median as the middle-most positional measure of central tendency. Construct cumulative frequency distributions (cf), locate the Median Class (where cf ≥ N/2), and apply the median formula: Median = l + [ (N/2 - cf) / f ] × h. Master the classical empirical relationship: 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean.
key_concepts: Cumulative Frequency (cf): The running cumulative sum of frequencies up to the upper limit of each class
Median Class: The class interval whose cumulative frequency is greater than (and nearest to) N/2, where N = Σ fi
Median Formula: Median = l + [ (N/2 - cf) / f ] × h
Variable Definitions: l = lower limit of median class, N = total frequency, cf = cumulative frequency of PRECEDING class, f = simple frequency of median class, h = class width
The Empirical Relationship: 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean (Allows finding any third measure given the other two!)
Ogive Intersection: The x-coordinate of the intersection point of 'less-than' and 'more-than' ogives gives the exact median
subtopics: Constructing cumulative frequency tables
Preceding cf vs simple f distinction
Empirical relationship calculations: Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean
Worked Example 7 and Example 8 from NCERT

worked_examples.problem:
Example 7 (NCERT): A survey regarding the heights (in cm) of 51 girls of Class X of a school was conducted and the following data was obtained:
Height: Less than 140 (4), Less than 145 (11), Less than 150 (29), Less than 155 (40), Less than 160 (46), Less than 165 (51).
Find the median height.
worked_examples.solution:
Given: 'Less than' cumulative frequency distribution with total girls N = 51.

Step 1: Convert into Continuous Class Intervals and calculate simple frequencies 'fi':
Interval 135-140: f1 = 4,   cf = 4
Interval 140-145: f2 = 11 - 4 = 7,  cf = 11
Interval 145-150: f3 = 29 - 11 = 18, cf = 29
Interval 150-155: f4 = 40 - 29 = 11, cf = 40
Interval 155-160: f5 = 46 - 40 = 6,  cf = 46
Interval 160-165: f6 = 51 - 46 = 5,  cf = 51.

Step 2: Find N/2 and locate the Median Class:
N = 51 ⇒ N / 2 = 51 / 2 = 25.5.
The cumulative frequency just greater than 25.5 is 29, which corresponds to the class 145 - 150.
Therefore, Median Class = 145 - 150.

Step 3: Extract parameters for Median Formula:
Lower limit of median class l = 145
Class size h = 150 - 145 = 5
Cumulative frequency of preceding class cf = 11 (from 140-145)
Simple frequency of median class f = 18.

Step 4: Apply Median Formula:
Median = l + [ (N/2 - cf) / f ] × h
Substitute values:
Median = 145 + [ (25.5 - 11) / 18 ] × 5
= 145 + [ 14.5 / 18 ] × 5
= 145 + 72.5 / 18
= 145 + 4.028 = 149.03 cm.

Step 5: Sanity Check:
149.03 cm lies strictly within the median class 145 - 150 (Valid!).
[ROUGH_WORK]
72.5 / 18 = 4.0277... ≈ 4.03 cm.
145 + 4.03 = 149.03 cm.
Boxed Answer: [ Median height = 149.03 cm ].
concept_questions: Why must cf be taken from the class preceding the median class?
What is the median class when N/2 = 25.5?

title: Exercise 13.1 Complete Solver: Grouped Mean Across 9 Practical Scenarios (Q1 to Q9)
description: Complete step-by-step resolution of NCERT Exercise 13.1 Questions 1 through 9. Covers plants in 20 houses (Q1), daily wages of 50 workers (Q2), missing pocket-money frequency 'f' with mean ₹18 (Q3), heartbeats of 30 women (Q4), packaging boxes with unequal class intervals (Q5), daily food expenditure of 25 households (Q6), SO2 concentration in 30 localities (Q7), student absenteeism days (Q8), and literacy rates of 35 cities (Q9).

worked_examples.problem:
Exercise 13.1 Q3: The following distribution shows the daily pocket allowance of children of a locality. The mean pocket allowance is ₹ 18. Find the missing frequency f.
Daily allowance (in ₹): 11-13 (7), 13-15 (6), 15-17 (9), 17-19 (13), 19-21 (f), 21-23 (5), 23-25 (4).
worked_examples.solution:
Given: Mean pocket allowance x̄ = ₹ 18.
Let us construct the table with Class Marks xi and deviations di = xi - 18:

Interval 11-13: x1 = 12, f1 = 7,  d1 = 12 - 18 = -6, f1·d1 = 7 × (-6) = -42
Interval 13-15: x2 = 14, f2 = 6,  d2 = 14 - 18 = -4, f2·d2 = 6 × (-4) = -24
Interval 15-17: x3 = 16, f3 = 9,  d3 = 16 - 18 = -2, f3·d3 = 9 × (-2) = -18
Interval 17-19: x4 = 18, f4 = 13, d4 = 18 - 18 = 0,  f4·d4 = 13 × 0 = 0
Interval 19-21: x5 = 20, f5 = f,  d5 = 20 - 18 = +2, f5·d5 = f × (+2) = 2f
Interval 21-23: x6 = 22, f6 = 5,  d6 = 22 - 18 = +4, f6·d6 = 5 × (+4) = +20
Interval 23-25: x7 = 24, f7 = 4,  d7 = 24 - 18 = +6, f7·d7 = 4 × (+6) = +24

Step 1: Compute Total Frequency Σ fi:
Σ fi = 7 + 6 + 9 + 13 + f + 5 + 4 = 44 + f.

Step 2: Compute Total Deviations Σ fi·di:
Sum of negative terms = -42 - 24 - 18 = -84
Sum of positive constant terms = +20 + 24 = +44
Net sum = -84 + 44 + 2f = 2f - 40.

Step 3: Apply Assumed Mean Formula (with a = 18):
x̄ = a + ( Σ fi·di ) / ( Σ fi )
Substitute x̄ = 18, a = 18:
18 = 18 + ( 2f - 40 ) / ( 44 + f )
Subtract 18 from both sides:
0 = ( 2f - 40 ) / ( 44 + f )

Step 4: Solve for f:
Since 44 + f ≠ 0:
2f - 40 = 0
2f = 40
f = 40 / 2 = 20!
[ROUGH_WORK]
By choosing the assumed mean 'a' to equal the given mean 18, the deviation sum must be identically zero! 2f - 40 = 0 ⇒ f = 20. Lightning fast!
Boxed Answer: [ Missing frequency f = 20 ].
concept_questions: Why does setting a = 18 reduce the equation to 2f - 40 = 0 instantly?
What is the total number of children when f = 20? (44 + 20 = 64)

title: Exercise 13.2 Complete Solver: Grouped Mode & Comparative Mean Analysis (Q1 to Q6)
description: Complete step-by-step resolution of NCERT Exercise 13.2 Questions 1 through 6. Covers hospital patient age mode vs mean (Q1), electrical component lifetimes (Q2), household expenditures (Q3), teacher-student ratios (Q4), runs scored by world batsmen (Q5), and passing car counts (Q6). Interpret why Mode and Mean differ.
key_concepts: Ex 13.2 Q1: Hospital patient ages: Modal class 35-45 (f1 = 23, f0 = 21, f2 = 14) ⇒ Mode = 36.8 years, Mean = 35.37 years
Ex 13.2 Q2: 225 electrical components: Modal class 60-80 (f1 = 61, f0 = 52, f2 = 38) ⇒ Mode = 60 + [9 / (122 - 90)] × 20 = 65.625 hours
Ex 13.2 Q3: Monthly expenditure: Modal class 1500-2000 (f1 = 40, f0 = 24, f2 = 33) ⇒ Mode = ₹1847.83, Mean = ₹2662.50
Ex 13.2 Q4: State teacher-student ratio: Modal class 30-35 (f1 = 10, f0 = 9, f2 = 3) ⇒ Mode = 30.6, Mean = 29.2
Ex 13.2 Q5: World batsmen runs: Modal class 4000-5000 (f1 = 18, f0 = 4, f2 = 9) ⇒ Mode = 4608.7 runs
Ex 13.2 Q6: Passing cars: Modal class 40-50 (f1 = 20, f0 = 12, f2 = 11) ⇒ Mode = 44.7 cars
subtopics: Full resolution of Exercise 13.2 Questions 1 to 6
Comparing central tendencies: Mode (most frequent) vs Mean (average balance)
Precise decimal rounding for modal values

worked_examples.problem:
Exercise 13.2 Q2: The following data gives the information on the observed lifetimes (in hours) of 225 electrical components:
Lifetimes (in hours): 0-20 (10), 20-40 (35), 40-60 (52), 60-80 (61), 80-100 (38), 100-120 (29).
Determine the modal lifetimes of the components.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Total components N = 225.

Step 1: Identify the Modal Class:
The maximum frequency in the table is 61, which belongs to the class interval 60 - 80.
Therefore, Modal Class = 60 - 80.

Step 2: Identify variables for Mode formula:
Lower limit of modal class l = 60
Class size h = 80 - 60 = 20
Frequency of modal class f1 = 61
Frequency of preceding class f0 = 52 (for class 40-60)
Frequency of succeeding class f2 = 38 (for class 80-100).

Step 3: Apply the Mode Formula:
Mode = l + [ (f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2) ] × h
Substitute values:
Mode = 60 + [ (61 - 52) / (2(61) - 52 - 38) ] × 20
= 60 + [ 9 / (122 - 90) ] × 20
= 60 + [ 9 / 32 ] × 20
= 60 + (180 / 32)
Divide 180 by 32 (or divide numerator and denominator by 4: 45 / 8):
45 / 8 = 5.625.
Mode = 60 + 5.625 = 65.625 hours.

Step 4: Sanity Check:
65.625 hours lies strictly inside the modal class 60-80 (Valid!).
[ROUGH_WORK]
2 × 61 = 122.
52 + 38 = 90.
122 - 90 = 32.
9 × 20 = 180.
180 / 32 = 5.625.
Boxed Answer: [ Modal lifetime of components = 65.625 hours ].
concept_questions: What does 65.625 hours represent in engineering terms? (The single most common lifetime period for the components)
Why does the mode lie closer to 60 than 80? (Because f0 = 52 is much larger than f2 = 38)

title: Exercise 13.3 Complete Solver: Dual Missing Frequencies (x, y) & Cumulative Ogives (Q1 to Q7)
description: Complete step-by-step resolution of NCERT Exercise 13.3 Questions 1 through 7. Master the celebrated board exam dual missing frequency problem where Median = 28.5 and N = 60 to find x = 8 and y = 7 (Q2), converting cumulative life insurance policies to continuous intervals (Q3), continuous class limit conversions with 0.5 adjustments (Q4), neon lamp median lifetime (Q5), surname letters mean/median/mode comparison (Q6), and student weights (Q7).
key_concepts: Ex 13.3 Q1: 68 consumers electricity: Median = 137 units, Mean = 137.05 units, Mode = 135.76 units

Ex 13.3 Q2: Landmark Missing Frequencies x and y: Total N = 60, Median = 28.5 (lies in 20-30). Equation 1: 45 + x + y = 60 ⇒ x + y = 15; Equation 2 from median formula: 28.5 = 20 + [(30 - (5 + x)) / 20] × 10 ⇒ x = 8 ⇒ y = 7!
Ex 13.3 Q3: Life insurance 'Below 20, 25...' conversion to 18-20, 20-25...: Median = 35.76 years
Ex 13.3 Q4: Leaf lengths (discrete 118-126, 127-135 continuous adjustment to 117.5-126.5...): Median = 146.75 mm
Ex 13.3 Q5: 400 neon lamps: Median = 3406.98 hours
Ex 13.3 Q6: 100 surnames: Median = 8.05 letters, Mean = 8.32 letters, Mode = 7.88 letters
Ex 13.3 Q7: 30 students weight: Median = 56.67 kg
Empirical Check: 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean holds across all distributions
subtopics: Full resolution of Exercise 13.3 Questions 1 to 7
The dual missing frequency algebraic system (x + y = 15)
Boundary continuity correction: Subtracting 0.5 from lower and adding 0.5 to upper limit

worked_examples.problem:
Exercise 13.3 Q2: If the median of the distribution given below is 28.5, find the values of x and y.
Class interval: 0-10 (5), 10-20 (x), 20-30 (20), 30-40 (15), 40-50 (y), 50-60 (5). Total frequency = 60.
worked_examples.solution:
Given:
Median = 28.5
Total frequency N = 60.

Step 1: Construct the Cumulative Frequency (cf) Table:
Interval 0-10:   f = 5,   cf = 5
Interval 10-20:  f = x,   cf = 5 + x
Interval 20-30:  f = 20,  cf = 25 + x  <-- Median Class
Interval 30-40:  f = 15,  cf = 40 + x
Interval 40-50:  f = y,   cf = 40 + x + y
Interval 50-60:  f = 5,   cf = 45 + x + y.

Step 2: Form Equation (1) from total frequency:
Total frequency = 45 + x + y = 60
x + y = 60 - 45
x + y = 15 ... (1)

Step 3: Identify the Median Class:
Since the median is given as 28.5, it lies strictly in the class interval 20 - 30!
Therefore, Median Class = 20 - 30.

Step 4: Extract parameters for Median Formula:
Lower limit l = 20
Class size h = 10
Total frequency N = 60 ⇒ N / 2 = 30
Cumulative frequency of preceding class cf = 5 + x (from 10-20)
Simple frequency of median class f = 20.

Step 5: Apply Median Formula:
Median = l + [ (N/2 - cf) / f ] × h
Substitute values:
28.5 = 20 + [ (30 - (5 + x)) / 20 ] × 10
Subtract 20 from both sides:
8.5 = [ (30 - 5 - x) / 20 ] × 10
8.5 = (25 - x) / 2
Multiply both sides by 2:
17 = 25 - x
x = 25 - 17 = 8.

Step 6: Find y from Equation (1):
x + y = 15
8 + y = 15 ⇒ y = 15 - 8 = 7.
[ROUGH_WORK]
Check total: 5 + 8 + 20 + 15 + 7 + 5 = 60 (Verified!).
Check median: 20 + [(30 - 13)/20] × 10 = 20 + (17/2) = 20 + 8.5 = 28.5 (Verified!).
Boxed Answer: [ x = 8, y = 7 ].
concept_questions: Why did we use Median = 28.5 to identify the median class instead of N/2 = 30? (Because cf contains unknown x, but 28.5 directly tells us the interval is 20-30!)
What is the value of x + y?

common_misconceptions: Forgetting the brackets around (5 + x) when writing 30 - cf: Writing 30 - 5 + x gives 25 + x, which produces a negative value for x! It MUST be 30 - (5 + x) = 25 - x!
Looking for N/2 = 30 in cf to find the median class: Since cf has variable x, you cannot locate 30 directly; you must look at the known median value 28.5.
